personas.name: Priya
personas.profile: Frontend lead of six engineers on one React app with a half kept up Storybook, on Chromatic today. She uploads each build from GitHub Actions and accepts or rejects each change on the build page; her goal is that every pull request shows what changed visually and nothing merges until someone has looked.

focus.review: One click from the pull request to the change, never two clicks to review.
focus.docs: An answer to why a baseline moved, so baselines never drift without anyone knowing why.
focus.cli: Few false alarms, with anti-aliasing and font hinting absorbed, so not every pull request shows a red X.

personas.name: Marcus
personas.profile: Platform engineer on a monorepo of about twenty packages (a design system, three apps and the docs) built under a task runner whose cache skips unchanged packages. His goal is one visual check per pull request across every package, without spending CI minutes on packages that did not change.

focus.review: Twenty subprojects with one change each shown as twenty changes in one place, not as twenty checks on the pull request.
focus.docs: A setup that fits the task runner he already has, without each package needing its own configuration.
focus.cli: A package the cache skipped never leaves a required check waiting forever.

personas.name: Lena
personas.profile: Design-system maintainer who owns the component library and its tokens, which product teams consume, so one change ripples into every app. Her goal is to catch a token or spacing regression before a consumer ships it, and to know which stories the change touched.

focus.review: A diff measured at the level of a region that comes with a note, and a way to accept a library-wide change in one step.
focus.docs: How to keep an intended change from producing noise on every story.
focus.cli: A violation flagged without a screenshot leaving her machine.

personas.name: Tomás
personas.profile: Engineer at a fintech or health company whose screenshots can show data that looks like customer data, where nothing leaves the network without security sign-off. His goal is visual review with every screenshot kept in-house, self-hosted with Docker or on a box inside the LAN.

focus.review: A self-hosted app with all of the hosted features, and no feature that works only on the hosted app.
focus.docs: Every outbound call listed and off by default, and a data flow written down that says plainly where data goes.
focus.cli: No SaaS call that is required to run it.

personas.name: Sam
personas.profile: Solo developer or small agency building client sites, often without Storybook, sometimes with Playwright tests and sometimes with only a URL. Sam wants to know in a minute whether a CSS change broke the other pages.

focus.review: A report that never claims more than it measured.
focus.docs: No sign-up wall and no heavy configuration between Sam and the first answer.
focus.cli: No setup, no account and no Storybook, and exit codes that CI can read.
